keyFindings.description: The clause written to answer my previous finding introduced a new false one, in the same operator-facing paragraph and in the direction that costs the operator the action. It reads 'which fits once the duplication is gone, and does not before it' and concludes 'So what was filling the disk is the duplication, and the already-running volumes fit because it is being removed.' Two things make that false, and I derived both from the files rather than carrying them. First, nothing removes it: fourteen lines above, the same paragraph says 'Nothing prunes /legion/scratch: it grows for the life of the issue, across every pod of it', and that is what the code does — EnsureScratch only makes directories, and the one rm in the rendered wrapper is `rm -rf -- <root>/g*` for plugin generations. The 5.5 GiB the paragraph cites as returned came back because a person deleted a role's copy by hand. Second, and worse for the general case: a production volume never held the duplication being described. At the merge base 2127101bddff the runtime sets a role container no GOCACHE, no GOMODCACHE and no BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR at all — the only TMPDIR it sets is fetchEnvironment's, the fetch container's own — and xdgCacheHome is podHome + '/.cache', the container's filesystem. So the 17 GiB with 14 GiB of per-role Go caches is this branch's own issue volume under an intermediate per-role layout that no shipped image ever produced. After the apply an already-running volume does not lose duplication; it gains the shared scratch. The operational consequence is the one the paragraph then disarms: an operator reading 'the already-running volumes fit because it is being removed' takes no step on an issue already near its 20 GiB, and the next sentence tells them the failure mode is silent. The fix is to drop the causal clause and keep the arithmetic, which is a complete argument on its own — 2.1 to 2.7 GiB measured on live volumes plus the shared layout's 8.5 GiB worst case stays inside 20 — and to mark the 17 GiB as this branch's own workspace under a layout no release shipped. If an operator does have an issue near full, the true remedy is deleting its stale /legion/scratch/<role> directories by hand, which is worth the sentence the false one occupies.

Two entries of the body's Not proven / risk list are mine, are marked 'Open as the round's finding', and are both answered at this head — and one of them carries the sentence I already conceded was wrong. Entry 24 still says the shipped example and docs:1135 write 20Gi; both read 50Gi at this head, which is the error I owned to the architect and which has now survived into the artifact a merger and an operator read before pinning a digest. Entry 25 still says flock is declared on PATH and nothing refuses an image that moved it; worker.Dockerfile's final step now refuses exactly that. Every other closed finding in that list carries a strikethrough and 'Fixed and resolved'; these two do not. I am fixing them in this round rather than reporting them, since they are my lines, and recording them here because the record should show that the false sentence outlived its own correction by a round.

fixedThisRound.flockPath: Answered, and better than either option I offered. Rather than loosening the script or threading a field, the image's final build step now resolves `flock` and refuses anything but /usr/bin/flock — `flock="$(command -v flock)"; test "$flock" = /usr/bin/flock` — beside the existing git, legion and gh pins, so the declaration and the use are held to one path at build time. I confirmed the step is in the final stage and the last RUN in the file, that `set -eu` makes a mismatch abort the build rather than warn, and that the only looseness runs the safe way: an image keeping /usr/bin/flock but shadowing it earlier on PATH fails the build though the absolute call would have worked.
fixedThisRound.volumeReach: The first half of my finding is answered: the paragraph now says the new size reaches volumes created after the apply and no others, that it rides in the Sandbox's volumeClaimTemplates evaluated at claim creation, and that an issue's Sandbox outlives its pods. That part is accurate and is what I asked for. The clause added around it is the finding above.
